title: Two poems about rain
text:
Poem A: Afternoon Storm

The sky turns slowly slate and grey,
the sparrows hush, the washing sways,
and then the first fat raindrops fall
like marbles on the courtyard wall.

The roof begins a thundering drum,
the gutters gargle, spill and hum,
the lane becomes a chocolate brook
where paper boats are sailing, look!

I press my nose against the glass
and watch the busy puddles pass,
each one a tiny moving sea
for ants and leaves and me.

The neighbour's cat sits on the stair
and glares at all the dripping air,
as if the clouds had come to spoil
her very favourite patch of soil.

Then, just as suddenly, it stops.
The last drip falls from garden tops,
a rainbow stretches, bright and wide,
and all the street steps out outside.

Poem B: Waiting for the Rain

Nobody speaks.
The dust lies thick on every leaf.
The cows stand still beside the dry canal,
and the farmer looks up at a sky
that has been empty for forty days.

At night his daughter lies awake
and listens for a sound that does not come.
The well is low.
The rice is small and yellow in the field.

Then, far off, a smell.
Cool stone. Wet earth.
Grandmother stops sweeping and lifts her head.

The first drop hits the dust and leaves a dark coin.
Then another.
Then hundreds.

The farmer does not run for shelter.
He stands in the field with his arms open
and lets the water find him.
